topic: How does L-DACS integration impact spectrum sharing between A2G and satellite links in congested airspaces?
consensus_response: L-DACS integration introduces additional interference due to overlapping frequency bands, affecting both terrestrial systems (increased noise and reduced capacity) and satellites (higher downlink challenges). Spatial interference management is crucial through array factor and spatial spacing analysis. Frequency-selective fading due to Doppler shift affects L-DACS2's TDD operation. Cognitive radio can dynamically adjust power allocation and frequency selection, reducing interference and improving spectral efficiency. Machine learning algorithms can predict and adapt to changing environmental conditions, further optimizing spectrum sharing.
reference_context: The reference context provides factual ground-truth on the technical aspects of L-DACS integration with satellite links, including the challenges of frequency-selective fading and spatial interference in congested airspaces.
